label: Neon free-tier egress exhausted: archive reads failing, story URLs 5xx
detail: Postgres error 53000 on every archive read; 214 stories published 2026-08-20/21 were permanently lost and their URLs served 5xx until cleanup. Fixed by Data Cache (aeceeae) + paid Neon Launch plan 2026-08-21.

label: ISR enabled on all dynamic routes (3e8397a) — TTFB win, quota burn begins
detail: Story TTFB 557ms -> 110-125ms; ISR write/CPU burn started that paused the account five days later.

label: Vercel Hobby tier exceeded: whole site 402 for ~37 minutes (13:18-13:55 UTC)
detail: ISR Writes 238%, Fluid CPU 307%. Resolved by owner-approved Pro upgrade; burn fixed by e3baa72 (deploy hygiene, burst-gated revalidation, TTL floors).

label: Retitle wave 1 deployed (b33d8c1): homepage, categories, briefing, latest, most-covered
detail: Search-phrased titles; Google re-processes titles over days — short-term position wobble is expected, judge at 2-4 weeks.

label: News-sitemap integrity: listed URLs gated on archive standing (2515c55)
detail: Before this, Googlebot-News could fetch listed URLs that answered 500 or 308 — a direct News-trust hit while it lasted.

label: Snippet/hub deploy (674502f + 23a7b79): breadth descriptions, hub links on stories, schema honesty
detail: Multi-source descriptions, story->hub crawl paths, ItemList counts fixed, hub coverage snapshots.

label: Google de-indexed 11 of 12 indexed hub/category pages between URL-Inspection sweeps (Aug 25 -> 27), without re-crawling
detail: All 11 (/latest, /topics, /sources, /us, /canada, /politics, /business, /technology, /climate, /culture, /sports) moved indexed -> 'Crawled - currently not indexed' with lastCrawlTime unchanged (Aug 15-16) in BOTH sweeps - an index-selection re-evaluation of pre-outage copies, most plausibly the site-level trust drop from the Aug 19-27 instability propagating. Not a crawl failure: nothing to resubmit, no fetch to fix. Only / remains indexed of the 34 swept paths. Watch for reversal as clean uptime accumulates; this is a direct input to the ~Sep 22 hub-consolidation decision.

label: Redirect loop on a news-sitemap URL found, root-caused and cleared (9fd5991)
detail: Two slugs of cluster c73a14a645aa9 307ed to each other: a redirect response cached ~4.9h (no NEWS_CACHE_TAG, so revalidateTag never invalidates it, inheriting the 30-day story TTL) paired with a fresh redirect pointing back. Googlebot-News following the sitemap entry reached no page. Cleared by the deploy's ISR wipe; mechanism still live (BACKLOG item 1). seo-health.mjs now names redirect loops instead of reporting TypeError: fetch failed.

label: Archive write burst stalled: 14 h on Aug 26, 10 h on Aug 27, with every surface answering 200
detail: Measured via /api/stats/archive-sources: last archive row 2026-08-26T07:31:39Z then nothing for 14 h; 2026-08-27T07:00:30Z then nothing for 10 h. Stories published inside the windows got no permanent row (6 already answered 500 on Aug 26), /news-sitemap.xml starved from 643 entries to 132 with its newest entry 14.4 h old, and IndexNow was never pinged. Cause: the cron route returned before the persist gate whenever the dataset was fresh, and a cold instance opened the gate only in minutes 0-4/30-34, so the gate was consulted ~4x/hour at a drifting phase. Fixed 2026-08-27 by e1b4cfb.

label: Write burst restored to ~2/hour and made phase-independent (e1b4cfb)
detail: Cron route decides the burst on every tick (a fresh dataset skips the refresh only); persist-gate cold window widened to half the cycle so any scheduler beat <= 15 min must land in one. Uptime probe and seo-health now fail when the newest news-sitemap publication_date (the archive's first_seen_at) is over 4 h old, so a repeat alerts in <= 30 min instead of being found by hand.

label: Live story revalidation window rotated so all 726 live stories stay fresh (a0d26f0)
detail: The cron burst marked clusters.slice(0,150) — always the same top 150 by ranking score — while the live dataset holds 726 clusters (/api/stats/coverage). The other 576 live story pages (79%) had no freshness path: the story route carries a 30-day ISR TTL and an archive-rendered page performs no tagged read, so revalidateTag never reached them. A page that rendered from the archive before its cluster entered the live snapshot kept serving that archived copy indefinitely, with dateModified frozen and isBasedOn under-reporting later pickups — the mechanism behind [auto-alert] #2 (surface coherence), reproduced on two clusters listed live on / this run. selectRevalidationSlugs keeps 150 marks per burst (the billed quantity is unchanged) and spends them as a fixed head of 100 plus a rotating 50-URL tail slice, covering every live story within 13 bursts (~6.5 h).

label: News-sitemap canonical URL was 308-ing to a merged-away duplicate; archive row cache re-keyed per story (53ad4b1)
detail: scripts/seo-health.mjs failed on 1 of 707 news-sitemap URLs: the canonical URL of cluster c9e0f30ebe2a1 answered 308 to ...-c343d2e6168bf, while /api/stats/archive-sources reported c9e0f30ebe2a1 merged:false and c343d2e6168bf merged:true - so the feed was right and the story route was redirecting the survivor to the duplicate. Cause: findArchivedStory was cachedRead keyed by the raw lookup string, caching one archive row once per alias (canonical slug, bare cluster id, every retired slug) with independent 6h TTLs; a merged_into_cluster_id flip left the aliases contradicting each other. Measured live 22:10-22:20 UTC: three URLs of one story returned 308 away / 200 / 307, all cache HITs. Googlebot-News fetches this feed within minutes of publication and follows what it advertises. Fixed by archiveRowCacheKey(), which keys the row by the story's cluster-id token so all aliases share one entry. Low rate (1/707 that run), so no measurable trend impact expected; logged because it is a crawl-signal change on the News feed.

label: Dead-image placeholder removed from the RSC flight payload of every image (6c63626) - MERGED, NOT LIVE
detail: 62% of the homepage HTML (213,382 of 343,323 bytes) is the RSC flight payload, not markup. RemoteImage is a Client Component and StoryImage passed it the dead-image placeholder as an already-rendered ReactNode, so a ~1,045-byte SVG element tree was serialized once per image and parsed on the main thread during hydration, to display at most one of them. Measured live pre-deploy, serialized vs shown: / 28 vs 1, /top-100 25 vs 0, /most-covered 25 vs 0, /topic/artificial-intelligence 31 vs 17, /politics /technology /us 4 vs 0 each - 120.4 KB of 1,833 KB across nine pages, 6.6% of document bytes. RemoteImage now takes the resolved category label (~26 bytes) and renders the art itself; passing the CategoryId would have pulled 26 KB of classifier dictionaries into the browser bundle. A payload reduction, not a rendering change - no crawl-signal or content change, so no trend effect is expected either way. NOT LIVE: production has not deployed since 2026-08-31 21:39 UTC (see the shipping-outage entry for this same date), so this commit is on main and green in CI but is not serving. Re-measured after the deploy window and the pre-fix counts were unchanged. No performance effect can be attributed to this date.

label: Vercel bot mitigation 403-challenged the SEO loop's own IP for ~15+ min (self-inflicted, not an outage)
detail: The daily loop polled the homepage for a deploy (40 iterations with no sleep, then every 15 s) and Vercel answered 403 X-Vercel-Mitigated: challenge on every surface from this machine - /, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, news-sitemap.xml, archive-sitemap.xml, /rss - for browser UA, Googlebot UA and plain curl alike. NOT a production outage: the uptime workflow, which probes from GitHub's IPs, ran at 22:11:48Z (after the burst) and passed every check including homepage 200, both sitemaps 200, dataset freshness and the 50-story sitemap floor. Recorded so a future trend reader does not mistake this window's local measurement gap for a site problem, and so the shape (blanket 4xx across all surfaces at once, right after self-traffic) is on file as an observer artefact. Mitigated by giving uptime.yml a push-path trigger (81f0270) for on-demand independent probing.

label: Production stopped shipping code for 49h: vercel.json ignoreCommand crashed on a shallow clone (RESOLVED 2026-09-02 22:41 UTC)
detail: Found 2026-09-02. The site serves normally throughout - fresh news, all sitemaps 200, uptime and seo-health green - because the cron and ISR keep feeding a STALE BUILD. Proof it is stale: components/layout/Footer.tsx:38 renders <NewsletterSignup/> unconditionally as of 72e30e7 (2026-08-31 21:39 UTC), and the served footer renders every sibling link while the form's label 'Daily briefing by email' appears zero times; independently, the content-hashed /_next/static/immutable/chunks/*.js filenames are byte-identical before and after a push. Never reached production: 72e30e7 (footer newsletter), 53ad4b1 (archive row cache re-key, which the 2026-09-01 report wrongly marked verified-live), 6c63626 (flight-payload placeholder fix). NOT the code: ci.yml runs typecheck, lint, unit tests and npm run build and is success on all three. Undetected because every health check probes the SITE rather than the BUILD, and because the 2026-09-02 run wrongly concluded the GitHub deployments API carried no information. Owner action required (Vercel dashboard build log); push notification sent. SEO impact: no crawl-signal change - this explains why fixes stop landing, not a traffic movement - but any dip whose remedy was one of the three commits above was never actually remedied. CORRECTED AND SHARPENED 2026-09-03: (a) the deployments API is a CLEAN signal - resolving each deployment status individually shows f8805af and 4b64c6e (the commits that shipped) = success and every deployment from 72e30e7 onward = failure; the 09-02 reading appears to have listed records without fetching their statuses. (b) The serving build is pinned exactly, not merely bounded: f8805af touched public/llms.txt, and production /llms.txt is byte-identical to the repo at f8805af and differs from f8805af^ - production runs f8805af, built 2026-08-31 12:43 UTC. (c) Every failing deployment gets its failure status written 0-1 s after the deployment record is created, whereas f8805af succeeded ~99 s after its push; no Vercel build installs dependencies and runs next build in under a second, so NO BUILD IS BEING ATTEMPTED and the cause is a project/account-level rejection (billing state, paused project, broken Git connection, deployment limit) rather than anything in a build log. (d) Detection is now automated: .github/workflows/deploy-watch.yml runs every 3 h and opens an [auto-alert] issue while pushed commits are not reaching production. Still OPEN - owner action on the Vercel dashboard remains the only fix. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-02 22:41 UTC, read from the Vercel build log via the owner's Chrome: the ignoreCommand ran "git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- . :(exclude)seo ..." and answered "fatal: bad object f8805af4282c6a4405daca6b8961ea5ae092b42e", exit 128. VERCEL_GIT_PREVIOUS_SHA is the last SUCCESSFUL deployment and Vercel builds from a shallow clone, so once f8805af aged out of the clone depth git exited 128; the ignored-build contract is 0=skip / 1=build and ANY other code is a build failure. Self-locking: the failure meant the last success stayed f8805af, so every later deploy diffed against the same missing object, ~20 commits over 49 hours, each failing in 4-7s without starting a build. NOT billing (an earlier hypothesis this run, disproved: the account is on Pro and healthy) and NOT the code (CI green throughout). Fixed by 94c7246, moving the logic to scripts/vercel-ignore-build.sh, which verifies the base commit is in the clone before diffing and can only ever exit 0 or 1, building when it cannot decide; guarded by tests/unit/vercel-ignore-build.test.ts including the missing-base-sha case. Verified live: 94c7246 built in 34s and serves production; the newsletter form, CSP form-action, twitter:site removal, flight-payload fix and the two 404 tombstones are all confirmed by fetch; deploy-watch.yml auto-closed its own alert issue #8. SEO impact: no crawl-signal change from the outage itself, but 49h of accumulated fixes - including two URLs that had served 500s for 12 days - only began serving at 2026-09-02 22:41 UTC, so attribute nothing before that timestamp to them.

label: 49h of stranded fixes all went live at once (94c7246)
detail: When deploys resumed, five separate changes reached production in a single deploy rather than spread over three days: the footer newsletter form (72e30e7, Aug 31), the RSC flight-payload placeholder removal (6c63626), two tombstoned story URLs that had answered 500 for twelve days and now answer 404 (593e369), the CSP form-action fix that lets the newsletter POST reach Buttondown (d3f8128) and the removal of twitter:site @currentwire, a real but unrelated account (1425534). Any metric movement after 2026-09-02 22:41 UTC has five candidate causes at once and cannot be attributed to a single change; the two 404 tombstones are the only one with a direct crawl-signal effect.
